title: kith-events: emit state changes from store operations
description:
What: Wire broadcast.send() into 8 store functions that advance state counters so listeners receive real-time notifications.

Algorithm:
The Store struct (after KITH-aai) has events_tx: Option<broadcast::Sender<StateChange>>. After each successful state advance, emit:
  if let Some(tx) = &self.events_tx { let _ = tx.send(StateChange { type_name: TYPE.to_string(), new_state }); }

Eight functions to modify (file: function - type_name - condition):
1. contact.rs: ContactStore::upsert() - "Contact" - always (called after advance_state())
2. contact.rs: ContactStore::set_blocked() - "Contact" - only if rows_affected > 0 (state was advanced)
3. chat.rs: ChatStore::get_or_create() - "Chat" - only if new rows inserted (state was advanced)
4. chat.rs: ChatStore::update_last_message_at() - "Chat" - only if rows_affected > 0
5. message.rs: MessageStore::insert() - "Message" - always (inside transaction, after counter advance)
6. message.rs: MessageStore::update_delivery_state() - "Message" - always (after advance_state_counter())
7. message.rs: MessageStore::update_read_at() - "Message" - always (after advance_state_counter())
8. outbox.rs: OutboxStore::mark_failed() - "Message" - after message counter advance; OutboxStore needs access to Store.events_tx (verify struct layout first)

Check how sub-store structs (ContactStore, ChatStore, etc.) are defined - if they are newtype wrappers over &Store, they can access self.0.events_tx; if they take &Connection, the events_tx must be passed as parameter.

Defensive rules:
- let _ = tx.send(...) always (SendError when no receivers is not an error condition)
- type_name strings: exactly "Contact", "Chat", "Message" (capital first; matches JMAP type names)
- Only emit after state is successfully advanced; never on error paths or no-op paths (rows_affected == 0)
- The send() is non-blocking (in-memory broadcast); safe to call while store mutex is held
